Stripped of the crown, and finally acting like the king Tindwyl trained him to be, Elend keeps working to save the city anyway. Cett is maneuvered into taking shelter inside Luthadel, which changes the balance outside it. Vin, increasingly convinced that the mist spirit she has glimpsed since Kelsier's day is real and that the prophecies of the Hero of Ages point at her, begins to suspect that someone close to the crew is passing information to their enemies, and that a kandra could be wearing the face of anyone she knows. Sazed and Tindwyl conclude that the altered inscription is not vandalism but a deliberate campaign of forgery reaching back a thousand years, carried out by something with the patience and the reach to edit written words themselves.

Vin takes the fight to Straff's camp, cutting through his defenses to reach him personally and leaving him convinced that she will kill him if he does not withdraw. The reprieve is brief. A third force appears: an army of twenty thousand koloss, the Lord Ruler's brutal, half-mad war creatures, brought south by Jastes Lekal, who has been buying their obedience with counterfeit coin that is beginning to fail. Luthadel cannot survive them. Vin's relationship with Zane comes to a head and she is forced to fight him; she kills him. In the aftermath, the kandra serving her confesses what he is: not the servant she believed, but an impostor who took that identity, sent to spy on her and ultimately to replace her. He refuses the last of his orders and tells her the truth instead, including the secret his people guard most closely, that a kandra can be controlled through the spikes driven into its body.

With the koloss army coming and no chance of holding the walls, Elend and the crew prepare for a siege they expect to lose. Sazed marries Elend and Vin. Vin, working through Sazed's research and the Lord Ruler's own account, realizes that the Well of Ascension is not in the distant northern mountains where every legend places it: the Lord Ruler built his palace on top of it, and it has been beneath Kredik Shaw the whole time. She also understands that the power gathering there is not infinite and will not wait, and that whatever wrote the false prophecies wants someone to reach it. The koloss break into Luthadel. The defense is desperate and the losses are heavy: Clubs and Dockson are killed in the fighting, and Tindwyl dies with them, leaving Sazed shattered. Elend is gravely wounded holding the line.

In the middle of the battle Vin draws power from the mists themselves, something no Allomancer is supposed to be able to do, and uses it to seize control of the koloss army outright, turning it against the forces besieging the city. Straff Venture is killed in the confrontation that follows and his army passes to Elend, who now commands the largest force in the Central Dominance despite having been voted out of his own throne. Luthadel holds. Carrying the dying Elend, Vin descends beneath the palace to the Well of Ascension and finds the power waiting for her exactly as the histories promised.

At the Well, Vin takes hold of the power and uses a fraction of it to heal Elend's wounds, which snaps him into Allomancy and leaves him a Mistborn. Then, as the inscription instructs and as Sazed's research seemed to confirm, she gives the power up rather than using it, believing that this is what the Hero of Ages is supposed to do. It is the one thing she should not have done. The prophecies were forged for precisely this purpose: the power at the Well was a prison, and releasing it frees Ruin, a god that has spent a thousand years altering every written record in the world to arrange its own escape. In the aftermath, Elend is crowned emperor and Penrod submits to him, Vin is hailed as the Hero of Ages by people who do not know what she has done, and Marsh, spiked through the body as all Inquisitors are, is no longer his own man. The kandra who served Vin returns to his people to answer for breaking his Contract. The ash falls more heavily than it has in living memory.

characters.description: The eldest Baudelaire, a fourteen-year-old inventor who ties back her hair to think and improvises devices to get her family out of danger. Having survived Count Olaf twice and lost two guardians, she remains the steady, protective leader of her younger siblings as they are moved to yet another home.
characters.name: Violet Baudelaire

characters.description: The middle Baudelaire, a twelve-year-old with glasses who reads voraciously and recalls what he learns. His knowledge has repeatedly saved the children, and he stays alert for Count Olaf, whom he no longer trusts any disguise to hide.
characters.name: Klaus Baudelaire

characters.description: The baby of the family, who speaks in short exclamations her siblings understand and whose four sharp teeth can bite through almost anything. Small but determined, she helps her brother and sister however she can amid the family's ongoing misfortunes.
characters.name: Sunny Baudelaire

characters.description: The greedy, murderous actor determined to steal the Baudelaire fortune, recognizable by his single eyebrow and the eye tattooed on his ankle. A relentless master of disguise, he has already murdered to reach the children's money and escaped capture twice, and the orphans expect him to appear again in some new false identity.
characters.name: Count Olaf

characters.description: The coughing banker who oversees the Baudelaire fortune and keeps relocating the orphans to new guardians. Kind in intention but hopelessly credulous, he rarely believes the children's warnings until it is too late.
characters.name: Mr. Poe

characters.description: The children's new guardian, the widow of a relative, who lives in a rickety house perched on stilts high above Lake Lachrymose. Obsessed with correct grammar, she is also gripped by countless fears, dreading such harmless things as the stove, doorknobs, and the telephone. Timid and easily frightened, she keeps her home cold and cheerless because she is afraid of the radiator, and her nervousness leaves the children feeling far from safe.
characters.name: Aunt Josephine

characters.description: A sinister sailor the family meets near Lake Lachrymose, distinguished by an eye patch and a wooden peg leg, who runs a sailboat rental business. Smooth-talking and eager to ingratiate himself, he showers attention on the fearful Aunt Josephine while treating the children with veiled menace.
characters.name: Captain Sham

recaps.ending: Aunt Josephine, who had gone into hiding to fake her own death, is discovered by the children in Curdled Cave, but her fearfulness dooms her: crossing Lake Lachrymose during Hurricane Herman, the boat is swarmed by the deadly Lachrymose Leeches, and Captain Sham forces the terrified Josephine overboard, where she is killed. Back on shore the Baudelaires expose Captain Sham as Count Olaf by revealing the eye tattoo hidden beneath his fake peg leg, but before Mr. Poe and the others can seize him, Olaf escapes once more. The children have lost another guardian, and their fortune remains the prize Olaf is determined to claim. Mr. Poe takes the orphans back into his care to place them somewhere new, while Count Olaf, exposed but uncaught, slips away to plan his next disguise and his next attempt on the Baudelaires and their money.
recaps.in_short: The Baudelaires are sent to live with fearful, grammar-obsessed Aunt Josephine, whose house teeters on stilts over Lake Lachrymose. In town they meet Captain Sham, a peg-legged sailor they recognize as Count Olaf in disguise, who charms the timid Josephine. Soon Josephine seems to throw herself out her great window into the lake, leaving a note naming Captain Sham as the children's new guardian. Noticing that the note is full of grammatical errors unthinkable for Josephine, the children decode them as a secret message and realize she is alive and hiding in Curdled Cave. During Hurricane Herman they sail across the leech-infested lake and find her, but on the way back the Lachrymose Leeches attack, and Captain Sham forces Josephine into the water to be devoured. On shore the children expose Sham as Olaf by revealing his ankle tattoo, but he escapes yet again. Aunt Josephine is dead, and the orphans are returned to Mr. Poe.

recaps.text: After a fire killed their parents, the Baudelaire orphans, inventor Violet, reader Klaus, and biting baby Sunny, inherited a fortune held in trust and were placed by the banker Mr. Poe with the cruel actor Count Olaf. Olaf tried to steal the money by forcing Violet into a fake marriage, then escaped when she foiled him. The children were next sent to their kind Uncle Monty, a herpetologist, but Olaf followed in disguise as an assistant named Stephano, murdered Monty, and nearly abducted them before the children exposed him; again he escaped, marked always by his single eyebrow and the eye tattooed on his ankle. Having lost two guardians and survived Olaf twice, the orphans are placed by Mr. Poe with yet another relative, fearing that Olaf will appear once more in some new false identity to pursue them and their inheritance.

Mr. Poe delivers the Baudelaires to Aunt Josephine, a nervous widow whose house sits on stilts high over Lake Lachrymose. Josephine is fanatical about correct grammar and terrified of an endless list of ordinary things, from the stove to doorknobs, so her home is cold and comfortless. On a trip into town for groceries the children meet Captain Sham, a sailor with an eye patch and a wooden peg leg who rents out sailboats. Despite his eagerness to befriend Josephine, the children recognize him as Count Olaf in disguise and are alarmed to see him worming his way into their fearful guardian's good graces. They try to warn Josephine and Mr. Poe, but the adults dismiss their suspicions, and the orphans realize that danger has once again followed them to their new home over the water.

Captain Sham continues to charm the anxious Aunt Josephine while the children's warnings go unheeded. Then disaster strikes: Josephine's great window is found shattered, and she appears to have thrown herself out into the lake below, leaving behind a note that makes Captain Sham the children's new guardian. The Baudelaires are grief-stricken but immediately suspicious, because the note is riddled with grammatical mistakes that the grammar-obsessed Josephine would never have made. Studying it closely, they conclude that the errors are deliberate, a hidden message left for them, and that their aunt may not be dead at all. As Captain Sham prepares to take custody of them, the children race to decode the note before they can be handed over to the man they know to be Count Olaf.

The children decipher the intentional errors in the note and discover that Aunt Josephine has faked her death and is hiding in Curdled Cave across Lake Lachrymose. With Hurricane Herman bearing down, they take a sailboat out onto the storm-tossed water, braving wind, waves, and the dreaded Lachrymose Leeches that live in the lake, and reach the cave. There they find Josephine alive but paralyzed by her fears, reluctant to leave her hiding place or to face Captain Sham. The Baudelaires persuade her to come with them, hoping to return safely and expose Sham as Count Olaf, but the crossing back across the churning lake will be far more dangerous than the journey out.

On the return voyage the Lachrymose Leeches, drawn by the fact that Josephine has recently eaten, swarm and attack the boat. Captain Sham appears in his own vessel, and rather than rescue Josephine he forces her into the water, where the leeches devour her. Back on shore, Sham tries to claim the children and their fortune, but the Baudelaires expose him as Count Olaf by revealing the eye tattoo hidden beneath his false peg leg. Confronted at last, Olaf escapes yet again before Mr. Poe can have him arrested, vanishing to plan his next scheme. Aunt Josephine, undone by her own fearfulness, is dead, and the orphans, having lost a third guardian, are returned to Mr. Poe's care to be placed somewhere new while Count Olaf remains free.

characters.description: A classless city runner known locally as the Windrunner. An independent wind gathers around her and assists her movement as she takes dangerous work near Raismelt.
characters.name: Ryoka Griffin

characters.description: A sickly information broker in Raismelt who secretly examines letters carried by runners. She keeps her true nature hidden at the inn where she lives.
characters.name: Young vampire

characters.description: A badly injured member of the Pithfire Hounds. Ryoka carries him to safety during an emergency delivery after bringing the trapped adventurers the potions they need, and his survival helps establish her as a dependable runner.
characters.name: Lamont

characters.description: The innkeeper of the Wandering Inn, a refuge for guests of many species. Her unusual inn, its magical door, and the household gathered around it remain central to her life near Liscor.
characters.name: Erin Solstice

characters.description: Erin's capable inn manager and Mrsha's guardian. She helps sustain the Wandering Inn as a home and shares responsibility for the young Gnoll.
characters.name: Lyonette

characters.description: A young mute Gnoll in the care of Erin and Lyonette. Recovering from earlier trauma, she is part of the close household formed around the Wandering Inn.
characters.name: Mrsha

characters.description: A member of Erin's chosen family who has a permanent home at the Wandering Inn.
characters.name: Bird

characters.description: A wounded Redfang Goblin bard and resident of the Wandering Inn.
characters.name: Numbtongue

characters.description: A fallen Goblin who took part in the defense of Liscor.
characters.name: Pyrite

characters.description: A Stitch Person alchemist based in Selim whose cloth body can be taken apart and repaired. Her business connection to the inn's magical door brings her to check on Erin while the inn is closed by grief.
characters.name: Octavia

characters.description: A Drake Wall Lord and established ally in Liscor.
characters.name: Ilvriss

characters.description: The half-elf leader of the Horns of Hammerad. She has unresolved business with the team's imprisoned former captain and the dungeon beneath Liscor.
characters.name: Ceria Springwalker

characters.description: The imprisoned former captain of Ceria's team. Disabled and awaiting judgment, he remains connected to the dungeon disaster and to the companions whose deaths and unfinished work continue to weigh on the Horns.
characters.name: Calruz

characters.description: Liscor's strategist.
characters.name: Olesm

characters.description: The necromancer formerly behind the Goblin Lord and a concealed danger to the Drake cities.
characters.name: Az'kerash

characters.description: A Japanese arrival from Earth and negotiator for the United Nations Company. His language skill and local contacts help hold together a precarious refuge made up of other Earth arrivals, former mercenaries, and local allies.
characters.name: Kenjiro Murata

characters.description: The Australian captain of the Bush Rangers, a silver-rank team using camouflage, traps, crossbows, and poisoned bolts. He seeks safer paid work for the United Nations Company while he and his teammates carry the effects of earlier battles.
characters.name: Dally

characters.description: A Swedish member of the Bush Rangers who specializes in camouflage. She joined the team after surviving apart from its original members.
characters.name: Siri

characters.description: An Australian aspiring writer who proposed supporting the United Nations Company by selling her romance fiction. She disappeared without a known resolution, leaving Dally with her unfinished work.
characters.name: Caroline

characters.description: A Dullahan adventurer who commands the silver-rank Rustless Guard. A dispute over an assignment ends when Dally offers her an honorable apology and a drink.
characters.name: Eldemar

characters.description: An Italian physician whose medicine is indispensable to the United Nations Company. Known locally as the Last Light of Boleros, she wants her work to support the group, though her value and limited protection make battlefield service especially dangerous.
characters.name: Geneva Scala

characters.description: The United Nations Company's treasurer and an inventive designer. She manages the group's dwindling shared funds, improves the Bush Rangers' crossbows, and looks for practical ways to preserve equipment brought from Earth.
characters.name: Paige

characters.description: A South African Olympic rowing hopeful who has turned his abilities toward courier work. He plans to earn income for the United Nations Company by carrying messages over water in a canoe.
characters.name: Luan

characters.description: An Italian arrival from Earth found malnourished after hiding from violent attackers. Her diabetes becomes an immediate danger because she has no insulin, leaving the rescuers to stabilize her until Geneva returns.
characters.name: Diana

characters.description: A traumatized New Zealand arrival from Earth rescued with three Italian survivors. He gives the Bush Rangers their first account of other Earth humans attacking the group with two young centaurs.
characters.name: Blake

characters.description: A distinct being sharing Geneva's living body. Able to control parts of that body with precision, the self-ed assists her medical work directly while remaining a separate presence with medical uncertainties of its own.
characters.name: Self-ed

characters.description: Geneva's nurse and surgical assistant. She supports the doctor's medical research and helps during emergency treatment, including a difficult operation to save a centaur mother and her child.
characters.name: Aiko

characters.description: A Minotaur planner who covertly hires Luan for a time-sensitive future delivery connected to the Titan's recurring game.
characters.name: Vanaz

characters.description: The Titan and head of the Forgotten Wing Company. Presented with unfamiliar nonmagical devices and reports about the United Nations Company, he privately concludes that people from another world are probably involved and begins an encrypted inquiry.
characters.name: Niers Astoragon

characters.description: A bee bonded to Lyonette and protective of her and Mrsha. It serves as a messenger and uses sustained flame-powered flight to outlast an attacking swarm's queen and claim territory.
characters.name: Lyonette's ashfire bee

characters.description: Liscor's Watch captain. She accepts Lyonette's plan to repay damage from earlier crimes and keeps the confiscated artifacts until the agreed fine is paid.
characters.name: Zevara

characters.description: A Gnoll bartender who owns Tails and Scales with his wife, Lassica. He comforts Erin and helps organize opposition to a concealed visitor fee.
characters.name: Rufelt

characters.description: A Drake chef who owns Tails and Scales with her husband, Rufelt. She comforts Erin and helps organize opposition to a concealed visitor fee.
characters.name: Lassica

characters.description: A skilled and expensive Drake scribe in Liscor. Olesm hires her to reproduce his strategy and chess publication, making her craft part of the effort to preserve and distribute the city's hard-won lessons.
characters.name: Ressa

characters.description: The King of Destruction and ruler of Rhyme. He enters Germina's succession as its foreign witness, offers its reborn ruler protected self-rule within his realm, and then takes Helios after its queen abdicates.
characters.name: Flos

characters.description: Flos's steward and left hand, responsible for turning conquest into administration. He prepares control arrangements for Germina and Helios and receives a desert clan whose young blacksmith has sworn to forge Flos an exceptional weapon.
characters.name: Orthenon

characters.description: An Earth-born teenage mage chosen as Flos's companion. Training under Rhyme's formidable vassals, he learns to cast Farsight without a staff while becoming involved with the arrival of a desert clan and its demanding oath.
characters.name: Trey

characters.description: An independent ruler formerly associated with Flos. At a neutral gathering of southern powers, she refuses to join opposition to him and commits her country to honoring his peace declaration and the return of those who claim his allegiance.
characters.name: Empress of Beasts

characters.description: The martial champion of a neutral sanctuary. The champion enforces its rules, refuses political killing, and ends a violent clash among visiting rulers without taking a life.
characters.name: Neutral sanctuary champion

characters.description: A Drake secretary who manages a neutral sanctuary. She secretly uses her document-copying ability to preserve the Emperor of Sands' proposal.
characters.name: Neutral sanctuary secretary

characters.description: A former mercenary captain allied with the United Nations Company. He urges the group to seek paid contracts, while recognizing that Geneva is too valuable and too poorly protected to serve safely as a battlefield doctor.
characters.name: Qualet

characters.description: A child incarnation who inherits Germina's cuirass office and memories while remaining a distinct person. As Germina's ruler, she accepts Flos's protection and an alliance that preserves her territory's self-rule within Rhyme.
characters.name: Reborn cuirass of Germina

characters.description: The only remaining smith in her desert clan able to work its rare metal. She arrives in Rhyme under an oath to forge Flos an exceptional weapon and bears responsibility for preserving the craft taught by her father.
characters.name: Desert-clan blacksmith

characters.description: A Lizardfolk sorcerer allied with the United Nations Company. After losing a foot in battle, she received a peg leg made by Geneva.
characters.name: Kexa

characters.description: A half-Gazer who puts Trey through demanding magical training. Under her instruction, he learns to cast Farsight without a staff.
characters.name: Ghazi

characters.description: The twin of Trey, from whom she has grown distant after a disagreement. They resume warmer contact and agree to speak privately as they begin repairing their relationship.
characters.name: Therese

recaps.ending:
The numbered story ends with Flos's peace declaration reshaping southern politics. Some rulers accept the demand to release his former subjects rather than risk war, while the Empress of Beasts refuses to join resistance against him. Her position leaves her isolated, and nine nations declare war on her country after a tense summit. The Emperor of Sands' copied proposal remains unexplained.

Elsewhere, Ryoka remains free and trusted by the concealed vampire family, whose illness and search for Rose, Imani, and Joseph remain unresolved. Lyonette runs the reopened Wandering Inn, Mrsha studies signs and magic, and Numbtongue holds Pyrite's memories, valuable mana stones, and unstable magicore. Ilvriss quietly investigates Az'kerash. The United Nations Company has new allies and medical prospects but still faces financial pressure, hostile Earth arrivals, fading memories, and Niers's attention. In the material following the numbered chapters, the long-range door proves too costly for regular travel, several visiting teams depart, and Ceria's Horns stay behind with the goal of reaching gold rank. The dungeon and Calruz's fate remain open.
recaps.in_short: Ryoka earns the name Windrunner through dangerous deliveries, befriends a hidden family of living vampires, and agrees to protect their secret while they search for missing Earth arrivals. In Liscor, Erin reopens her inn after the Goblins' deaths, recognizes Numbtongue as family, and leaves Lyonette to manage their growing home. Numbtongue inherits Pyrite's memories and hazardous mining knowledge. The United Nations Company rescues stranded Earth arrivals and wins allies through adventuring and Geneva's medicine, but remains poor, traumatized, and threatened by hostile Earth humans, fading memories, and Niers's secret inquiry. Ilvriss confirms that Az'kerash lives and begins a covert investigation. Flos adds Germina and Helios to Rhyme, expands weapons production, and demands safe passage for anyone claiming his allegiance. Nine nations then declare war on the Empress of Beasts. Afterward, visiting adventuring teams leave Erin's inn, while Ceria's Horns remain and resolve to pursue gold rank.

recaps.text: Previously: Erin Solstice established the Wandering Inn near Liscor as a refuge whose guests cross ordinary boundaries of species and allegiance. Lyonette helps run the inn and care for Mrsha, a young mute Gnoll, while Redfang Goblins including Numbtongue became part of its community. The struggle around Liscor ended with Goblins dying in the city's defense, leaving Erin and the survivors in grief. Ceria Springwalker leads the rebuilt Horns of Hammerad, but the team's former captain Calruz remains imprisoned after the dungeon disaster. Wall Lord Ilvriss has become an ally in Liscor, while the necromancer Az'kerash remains a concealed threat. Elsewhere, Earth arrivals have been scattered across the world. Ryoka Griffin works as a classless runner, and a mixed group of other arrivals and local allies has begun forming the United Nations Company.

Ryoka's northern work earns her the name Windrunner. She rescues the trapped Pithfire Hounds, then discovers that a Raismelt broker belongs to a hidden family of living vampires. The family cannot compel her silence, but she promises it freely after learning that they survive on animal blood and suffer a worsening inherited illness or curse. Ryoka and the young vampire become friends, and Ryoka asks her to search for Rose, Imani, and Joseph.

At the Wandering Inn, Erin's grief initially shuts out Liscor. Numbtongue openly challenges the city's treatment of the Goblins who defended it, buries Pyrite, and begins receiving the dead Goblin's memories. Erin names Lyonette, Mrsha, Numbtongue, and Bird as family, reopens the inn, and prepares to travel while Lyonette takes charge. Numbtongue gains public recognition as an adventurer and chooses the inn as his home.

The United Nations Company is nearly out of money. Dally's Bush Rangers become its main adventuring income, rescue four starving Earth arrivals, and learn that other Earth humans attacked them. Geneva returns to treat the newcomers. When giant serpents escape a dungeon, Dally delays them and Ken mobilizes local forces. Geneva then saves a centaur mother and child through emergency surgery. These successes win goodwill and an alliance with the indebted Rustless Guard, but the company remains financially fragile.

The United Nations Company searches for a sustainable future. Geneva considers a clinic and develops uncertain antibacterial treatment, while Paige confirms she can make gunpowder and the group secretly plans nonmagical grenades. Aiko and Luan recognize that Earthworlders are losing memories of their families. Luan tattoos his wife and son's names on his arm, continues earning money as a water courier, and accepts a covert delivery connected to the Titan's recurring game. Niers Astoragon examines Earth devices, concludes that another world's people are present, and opens a private investigation.

Lyonette expands her control of the Wandering Inn, negotiates restitution for her old crimes, teaches Mrsha more signs, and strengthens her bond with an ashfire bee. Erin visits another walled city through the magical door, where she finds a concealed visitor fee and a law that would kill Numbtongue if he entered. Sympathetic tradespeople begin challenging the fee. Numbtongue uses Pyrite's inherited mining knowledge to find mana stone and magicore, but his music transforms the material into an unstable electrical hazard.

Ceria visits Calruz in prison. He accepts responsibility for his actions and continues mapping the dungeon while expecting execution.

Flos enters Germina's succession ritual as the required foreign witness and protects its newly reborn child ruler. She accepts self-rule within Rhyme, and they agree to stop creating new child assassins. Flos then takes Helios after its queen abdicates, offering her son a chance to earn the kingdom's restoration through service. These settlements enlarge Rhyme but leave both territories unstable.

A desert clan reaches Rhyme under Orthenon's protection. Its young blacksmith proves her rare purification craft by forging a superior individual blade. Flos preserves the resident master smith's position because his work can equip an army, while commissioning the clan for exceptional weapons. He adopts a growth edict despite the pressure it will place on resources, judges that a coalition is his chief danger, and sends a continent-wide peace ultimatum. He promises not to attack states that leave him and his subjects alone, but demands safe release and passage for anyone who claims allegiance to him.

The ultimatum forces rulers to choose between losing experienced subjects and provoking Flos. At a neutral southern sanctuary, the Empress of Beasts refuses to join an anti-Flos alignment and agrees to honor his demand. The sanctuary's champion ends a violent confrontation without killing anyone. Its secretary secretly copies a proposal from the Emperor of Sands, but the contents remain unknown. The next day, nine southern nations declare war on the Empress of Beasts' country, opening a new conflict as Flos's expanding realm continues to prepare for wider war.
